title: Build Your Own Onion Routing Network
goal: Build and diagnose a multi-hop onion circuit, then defend exactly which observer can learn which facts from its traffic.

modules.title: Choose a path and name the observer
modules.goal: Choose a three-relay path and distinguish a relay’s local view from the simulator’s complete view.
modules.artifact: selectPath returns three distinct usable relay IDs or reports NO_PATH.
modules.difficulty: Directory filtering, distinctness and observer scope interact; crypto is not introduced yet.

modules.title: Wrap the onion from the destination outward
modules.goal: Construct a nested authenticated packet that each relay can open exactly one layer at a time.
modules.artifact: wrapRequest builds the entry packet using a separate forward key for each hop.
modules.difficulty: Nested values, reverse construction order, key scope and associated data interact.

modules.title: Forward one layer and bring the reply back
modules.goal: Open a single local instruction and build the reverse encryption path for the archive reply.
modules.artifact: peelForward, addReturnLayer and unwrapReply complete an offline round trip.
modules.difficulty: Forward removal and backward addition run in opposite directions; state belongs to one relay.

modules.title: Separate authenticity from freshness
modules.goal: Reject changed and repeated packets while preserving receiver state when authentication fails.
modules.artifact: acceptSequence and peelForward enforce bounded, circuit-local replay tracking.
modules.difficulty: Authentication order, state mutation and out-of-order valid arrival must remain distinct.

modules.title: Rebuild after a failed hop
modules.goal: Choose a valid replacement circuit and explain why retrying cannot prove exactly-once delivery.
modules.artifact: recoveryPlan chooses rebuild or stop; supplied lifecycle closes the old circuit and generates fresh keys.
modules.difficulty: Availability, key lifecycle and uncertainty about endpoint receipt interact.

modules.title: Challenge the privacy claim
modules.goal: Use synthetic timing evidence and endpoint observations to state defensible limits on an onion circuit.
modules.artifact: correlate returns all compatible timing candidates; the capstone combines the working circuit with an evidence report.
modules.difficulty: A compatible pattern is evidence, not identity; multiple observers and endpoint content differ.

status: local construction; browser acceptance NOT_RUN; not published
